sections.title: Risk Factors
text: An investment in the Ordinary Shares involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the following information about these risks, together with the other information appearing elsewhere in this prospectus, before deciding to invest in the Ordinary Shares. The occurrence of any of the following risks could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations, and future growth prospects. In these circumstances, the market price of the Ordinary Shares could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment.

The sustainability of our growth is contingent upon our ability to retain existing customers, attract new users, and encourage both groups to expand their engagement with our platform. To maintain our competitive position, we must continue to provide secure, reliable, and leading-edge technologies while offering competitive rates in an increasingly crowded and price-sensitive market. There is no assurance that we will successfully maintain our current growth trajectory or continue to grow at all. Our business is currently subject to significant customer concentration risk, as approximately 96.70%, 69.40% and 60.06% of our total processed volume for the six months ended April 30, 2026 and the fiscal years ended October 31, 2025 and 2024 were derived from two primary customers, respectively.

Our customers, including these primary counterparties, have no long-term obligation to continue using our services. Our standard business contracts typically include termination clauses that allow counterparties to terminate the relationship at any time or following a limited notice period. Furthermore, the complexity and costs for a customer to switch transaction volumes to a competitor may not be significant, particularly for larger customers who often maintain relationships with multiple payment service providers simultaneously to ensure redundancy.

• Approximately 35% for expansion into new geographical markets and jurisdictions, including selective entry into new cross-border payment corridors and strengthening local operational and compliance capabilities;

• Approximately 30% for development and enhancement of our AI-enabled risk and compliance intelligence platform to improve transaction monitoring, risk assessment and operational efficiency across our regulated payment operations;

The following sets forth a summary of the principal Singapore laws, regulations, and rules relevant to our business and operations in Singapore.

The MAS regulates the provision of payment services in Singapore under the Payment Services Act 2019, which came into force on January 28, 2020 (the “PS Act”). Unless exempted, any entity carrying on a business of providing regulated payment services in Singapore is required to obtain the appropriate license under the PS Act. Regulated payment services include, among others, account issuance services, e-money issuance services, domestic money transfer services, cross-border money transfer services, merchant acquisition services, digital payment token services and money-changing services.

The PS Act provides for three categories of licenses: (i) money-changing license, (ii) standard payment institution license and (iii) MPI license, with major payment institutions subject to more extensive regulatory requirements due to the scale of their operations.

revenue.heading: Revenue
revenue.text:
Our revenue increased by 17.4% to US$504,893 (of which US$10,511 was from related parties) for the six months ended April 30, 2026, from US$430,197 for the six months ended April 30, 2025. Although revenue directly derived from cross-border transaction processing volume decreased by 14.3%, the reduction was more than offset by an expansion in our exchange gain on currency exchange margins, driven by higher spread capture and better execution. In addition, we started to recognize revenue from consultancy service in the second half of 2025, from Regalrare Pte. Ltd., a related party, which accounted for 2.1% of our total revenue for the six months ended April 30, 2026.

Customer concentration remained significant during the period. Revenue generated from our largest customer, Customer A, increased by 33.4%, or US$106,925, to US$426,827 for the six months ended April 30, 2026, from US$319,902 for the six months ended April 30, 2025. Customer A accounted for 84.5% and 74.4% of our total revenue for the six months ended April 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

For the six months ended April 30, 2026, cash provided by operating activities was US$602,368. The net cash inflow was primarily attributable to the net loss of US$293,683, as adjusted by (A) adjustments to reconcile net loss to cash provided by operating activities including (i) deducting reversal of allowance of credit losses of US$105,985; and (ii) adding back deferred income tax of US$17,644; and (B) changes in operating assets and liabilities including (i) decrease in accounts receivable of US$15,829; (ii) decrease in receivables from payment processors, net of US$580,021; (iii) increase in deposits and prepayments of US$231,292; (iv) decrease in interest receivable from loan to a related party of US$118,404; (v) decrease in other receivable of US$33,397; (vi) decrease in amount due from a director of US$441,211; (vii) decrease in due from a related party of US$7,142; (viii) increase in accounts payable of US$30,609; (ix) decrease in accrued expenses and other payables of US$17,200; and (x) increase income tax payable of US$6,271.

For the six months ended April 30, 2025, cash provided by operating activities was US$716,176.

net.heading: Net income (loss)
net.text: Net income was US$846,195 for the year ended October 31, 2025, from a net loss of US$96,652 for the year ended October 31, 2024. While we incurred a loss from operations during fiscal year 2025, which reflected our strategic investments in professional fees, corporate restructuring, and compliance scaling, our overall net profitability was heavily bolstered by non-operating activities. Specifically, this transition to positive net income was primarily driven by other income, mainly the realized gain on digital intangible assets.

gp.heading: Gross profit and gross profit margin
gp.text:
Our gross profit increased by 58.5% to US$252,426 for the six months ended April 30, 2026, from US$159,241 for the six months ended April 30, 2025. Gross profit margin for the corresponding years is 50.0% and 37.0%, respectively.

General and administrative expenses primarily consist of operating expenses for director remuneration, staff salaries, business development expenses, consultancy fee, professional services fee, platform fee, rental expenses, bank service charges and other miscellaneous administrative expenses. Our general and administrative expenses increased by 438.8% to US$543,191 (of which US$12,176 was from related parties) for the six months ended April 30, 2026, from US$100,817 (of which US$11,177 was from related parties) for the six months ended April 30, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to professional fees and expenses incurred in connection with the Company’s initial public offering to support its capital-raising activities.
